channel.title: LoopRails, Human-in-the-Loop & AI Agent Safety
channel.description: Practical, sourced writing on human-in-the-loop oversight of AI agents, when review helps, when it's a rubber stamp, and how to design oversight that actually catches mistakes.

item.title: What Is Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) in AI?
item.description: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) means a person helps make or review an AI system’s decisions.

item.title: Does Human-in-the-Loop Improve AI Safety?
item.description: Human review can improve safety when reviewers know what to check, have the evidence and can act in time.

item.title: In-the-Loop vs On-the-Loop vs Out-of-the-Loop
item.description: These terms describe when a person can step in.

item.title: When Should an AI Agent Ask for Approval?
item.description: Ask for approval when an action needs permission or a reviewer can catch a costly mistake.

item.title: The Lethal Trifecta: How AI Agents Leak Data
item.description: Private data, untrusted content and a way to send data out create a dangerous combination.

item.title: AI Agent Guardrails: A Practical Checklist
item.description: Guardrails check an agent’s decisions and limit what its tools can do.

item.title: AI Agent Autonomy Levels (L0-L6)
item.description: Autonomy defines what an agent may do without asking.

item.title: Prompt Injection Prevention
item.description: Prompt injection hides malicious instructions in material an agent reads: pages, emails, documents, code or tool results.

item.title: Maker-Checker (Four-Eyes) for AI Agents
item.description: In maker–checker review, one party proposes an action and another authorizes it.

item.title: Automation Bias: Why People Rubber-Stamp AI
item.description: Automation bias means relying too much on automated advice.

item.title: How to Build an AI Kill Switch
item.description: A kill switch blocks new work and tries to stop work already running.

item.title: Study: How AI Agent Skills Leak Credentials
item.description: A 2026 study sampled 17,022 skills from SkillsMP and identified 520 affected skills containing 1,708 security issues.

item.title: Study: A Compiler as the Verifier
item.description: ComPilot uses a language model to propose loop transformations, then receives compiler legality checks and measured performance as feedback.

item.title: Agentic Loops in the Wild: Wins, Failures, Cost
item.description: An agent’s reported success depends on its task, tools, checks and budget.

item.title: AI Agent Sandboxing
item.description: A sandbox limits where an agent can act: the files it can access, programs it can run, services it can reach and resources it can use.

item.title: Least Privilege for AI Agents
item.description: Give an agent the access its task needs, for only as long as it needs it.

item.title: The Circuit Breaker Pattern for AI Agents
item.description: A circuit breaker blocks new work when a limit is reached.

item.title: What Is Agentic AI?
item.description: An AI agent uses a model to choose actions toward a goal.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Coding Agents
item.description: Give a coding agent a restricted workspace to explore and edit.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Customer Support
item.description: Let a support agent answer questions within its approved scope.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Financial Transactions
item.description: Check who can authorize a payment, where it will go and how much the agent can spend before moving funds.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Database Operations
item.description: Treat generated SQL as executable code.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Email & Messaging
item.description: Keep drafting separate from sending.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Deployments
item.description: Approval decides whether a release goes ahead.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Content Moderation
item.description: Automate routine moderation where the policy is clear and the cost of mistakes is understood.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for Machine Learning
item.description: People help train models by labeling examples, choosing useful training cases and rating outputs.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI in Healthcare
item.description: Assess clinical actions by their effect on patients.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Legal Work
item.description: AI can extract clauses and draft changes.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Hiring
item.description: Use AI to organize hiring evidence.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for Browser & Computer-Use Agents
item.description: Reading a page, filling a form and submitting a purchase need different controls.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for AI Voice Agents
item.description: Voice-agent controls need to work during a live conversation.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop for Multi-Agent Systems
item.description: A team of agents shares work, state and handoffs.

item.title: The LoopRails Doctrine
item.description: Build a loop that checks whether the work is useful.

item.title: What Is Loop Engineering?
item.description: Loop engineering designs how an AI agent acts, checks its work and chooses what to do next.

item.title: How to Build Your First Agent Loop
item.description: Start with one task, clear limits and a completion check the agent cannot bypass.

item.title: Loop Patterns for Engineering & Data Science
item.description: Choose a loop with a clear completion check and recovery plan.

item.title: Evaluation-Driven Development
item.description: Build the checks as you build the agent.

item.title: What Makes a Verifier Work
item.description: A verifier checks a claim about an artifact or state.

item.title: The Two Loops: Intent Clarity & the Delivery Gap
item.description: An agent loop tries to produce work that passes a check.

item.title: Oversight for Autonomous Loops
item.description: Check both the result and the route taken to produce it.

item.title: Context Engineering for Agent Loops
item.description: Context engineering chooses what the model sees on each turn: its goal, limits, current state, tools, evidence and recent results.

item.title: Loop Health: What to Monitor in a Running Loop
item.description: Watch progress, costs and changes to the world outside the agent.

item.title: World Models for Agent Loops
item.description: A world model predicts what may happen after an action.

item.title: Failure Recovery for Agent Loops
item.description: Check what happened before retrying.

item.title: Multi-Agent Loops: When More Agents Help
item.description: Several agents can research separate sources or work on different files at once.

item.title: MCP and Skill Overload
item.description: Tools and skills give agents more ways to act.

item.title: Agent Workflow Patterns
item.description: Use a workflow when you know the steps in advance.

item.title: Autonomous Agent Patterns
item.description: An autonomous agent checks the current state, chooses an action, uses a tool and examines the result.

item.title: RAG Retrieval Patterns
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) gives a model external evidence before it answers.

item.title: Advanced and Agentic RAG
item.description: Add retrieval steps when a simpler search misses evidence you need.

item.title: LoRA vs Fine-Tuning vs Pre-Training
item.description: Model adaptation changes a model’s learned behavior.

item.title: What You Can & Can't Do With Models You Don't Control
item.description: How you access a model determines what you can change.
